sections.0.body.0.t: Continuous Integration (CI) is the practice of automatically validating every code change: on each push or pull request, the pipeline compiles the project and runs the tests. The goal is to find out in minutes, not weeks, that a change broke something.

sections.0.body.1.t: Continuous Delivery/Deployment (CD) extends the pipeline all the way: the validated artifact is packaged and published. In continuous delivery, deploying to production still requires a human click; in continuous deployment, everything that passes the gates goes live on its own.

sections.1.body.0.t: Names vary between tools, but almost every pipeline follows the same backbone:

sections.1.bullets.0.t: source: a push or PR triggers the pipeline from the repository

sections.1.bullets.1.t: build: compiles, installs dependencies and resolves what the code needs

sections.1.bullets.2.t: test: unit tests, integration tests and security checks

sections.1.bullets.3.t: package: produces the final artifact: binary, package or container image

sections.1.bullets.4.t: deploy: publishes to staging and, afterwards, to production

sections.1.bullets.5.t: monitor: observability, alerts and a rollback path

sections.2.body.0.t: Abstraction turns into clarity when you see the pipeline written out: the workflow below is a real GitHub Actions pipeline, with the trigger (source), build, tests and a security check running as just another step.

sections.2.code.0.code.t:
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]        # source stage: what triggers it
permissions:
  contents: read                # least privilege for the pipeline token
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci                # build: reproducible install
      - run: npm test              # test: the test suite
      - run: pipx run semgrep scan --config auto --error   # security as one more step
      - run: docker build -t app . # package: produces the artifact

sections.3.body.0.t: Each stage is a gate where a security check can come in: SAST and SCA at build, DAST in staging, secrets scanning at source. This is what DevSecOps exploits.

sections.3.body.1.t: The reverse also holds: whoever controls the pipeline controls what goes to production. The SolarWinds attack (2020) compromised exactly the build system: the pipeline became the malware's distribution vector. The pipeline is critical infrastructure.

sections.3.heading.t: Why it is the center of security

short.t: The automated build, test and deploy pipeline

tagline.t: The backbone of modern software: every commit becomes a build, a test run and a deploy with no manual intervention.
